EU AI Act dates moved.

Logging, documentation, and human oversight didn't get optional.

That's the useful reading for banks and fintechs — not a race to stamp "AI Act compliant" on a landing page (we won't; you shouldn't trust vendors who do without proof).

Practical posture for governance teams:

• Treat evidence as the product: prompts, retrieved context, model versions, actions, approvers
• Watch RBI draft MRM (Jun 2026) as a board signal on AI/ML and third-party models — prepare exportable artifacts, don't wait for a logo seal
• For UAE LFIs: inventory, oversight, and clear data paths remain the conversation (CBUAE AI/ML guidance discourse — not a Sanctum "approval" claim)

We are not saying Sanctum makes you compliant with the EU AI Act, RBI, or CBUAE. We are saying: if your GenAI path can't show an audit trail you can export, the next regulatory or board cycle will ask why.

Start with a risk-scored Assess on one high-impact workflow. Build the evidence habit before the pilot hardens the wrong architecture.

• KYC / onboarding packages inside your boundary

• Exportable trail: what was asked, what was retrieved, which model version, who approved

Can you export every prompt, retrieved passage, and model version?

If the answer is “the vendor has logs” or “it’s in the SIEM somewhere,” model risk and internal audit will keep blocking production — even when the demo looked fine.

For credit, KYC, and policy copilots, governance needs artifacts you can hand over, not a slide that says “auditable.”

Minimum fields worth insisting on:
• Prompt (what was asked)
• Retrieved passage (what the system used)
• Model version (what answered)
• Action taken (what changed in the workflow)
• Approver / human review (who signed off)

Sanctum is designed so those fields are exportable — immutable audit as a product behavior, not a brochure claim. We don’t invent SOC 2 seals or “RBI-approved” badges. We show you what the trail records.
